data.gender_notes: Hurley is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Irish word 'O'hUrghail' meaning 'descendant of the dark-haired one'. In the Irish legend of Fionn Mac Cumhaill, Hurley was a champion warrior with dark hair. The name Hurley carries the meaning “Strong, Dark-haired One” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hurley usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, dark-haired one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hurley belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong, Dark-haired One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hurley total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hurley, though originating from Irish heritage, has gained popularity beyond its cultural roots. It has been adopted as an English surname and given name. In the English-speaking world, it is often associated with athleticism due to the famous name and professional surfing family, the Hurleys. The lasting impact of this family, particularly those that excel in surfing, has influenced the perception of the name as representing a free-spirited, adventurous, and talented individual.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hurley holds spiritual significance as it is rooted in the legacy of Fionn Mac Cumhaill, the legendary Irish warrior, and his dark-haired descendant. Hurley represents the heritage of those who hold their ancestry and traditions dear, yet embrace the confidence, determination, and tenacity embodied by this ancient hero. The name evokes a sense of connection to one's roots, encouraging introspection, and emphasizing personal strength and resilience.
